cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Get It on the Record
cards.instruction: Get formal approval, endorsement, or acknowledgment before anyone can quietly revise their position.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Before I pay the builder, will you sign that my fence can stay on our boundary?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Could you put 'can stay' beside your name? The builder won't invoice 'suppose.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want to promise forever.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Date it today, then. If you change your mind, we'll know which permission changed.

mechanism: A uses its former pupil careful wording as grounds to demand a dated boundary permission while accepting that consent need not last forever.
confusable: Not forcing eternal agreement: the record must identify the present permission before later revision.
comparison: Adversarial prior festival reversal versus accommodating a neighbor former pupil fear of permanent commitment.
